question: Not shared. P-96 screens cross-sectionally for currently present MMSE-defined cognitive impairment (>= 1 SD below the age-stratum mean MMSE) in the general CHARLS 2015 older population. P-166 predicts incident MCI over four years among CHARLS respondents with sarcopenia who were cognitively normal at baseline (21-point battery plus no IADL disability). Detecting present impairment in the general population and predicting future MCI in a baseline-normal sarcopenic subgroup are different tasks, comparisons and populations. The channel (clinical/tabular) is shared.

figures.P-96: RF on 7 routine variables: training set, stratified 5-fold CV (n=2932): AUROC 0.93 (95% CI 0.91-0.95); external Yiwu 2021: 0.83 (0.82-0.84); external CHARLS 2011: 0.87 (0.86-0.88). Intervals as printed.
figures.P-166: Test (20% of 414): 0.708 (95% CI 0.544-0.844); temporal validation CHARLS 2015-2018 (n=156): 0.711 (0.588-0.823). Intervals as printed.

matched_figure_check: Neither paper reports the other's endpoint (P-96 has no incident-MCI result, P-166 no prevalent-impairment result), so no matched figure can reconcile or confirm the gap. On validation tier alone the gap persists: P-96's external CHARLS 2011 0.87 (0.86-0.88) does not overlap P-166's temporal validation 0.711 (0.588-0.823).
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: P-96's 0.93 is below 0.97, from 2932 participants with two external cohorts; P-166 is 0.71.
reason: The intervals exclude each other, but the two AUCs answer different questions: detection of present MMSE-defined impairment in the general population (P-96) versus four-year prediction of incident MCI among cognitively normal sarcopenic adults (P-166). Condition 1 fails, so the gap is not a discrepancy on a shared clinical question.
